statement: The logit or log-odds function is defined for a probability p in (0, 1) as the logarithm of the odds p / (1 - p), or equivalently as the inverse of the standard logistic function sigma(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-x)): logit(p) = sigma^(-1)(p) = ln(p / (1 - p)). The supplied sources define this transformation directly and contain no derivation of it.

symbols.meaning: logit or log-odds of probability p
odds ratio between two probabilities p_1 and p_2

properties.property: Alternative algebraic formulations: logit(p) = ln(p) - ln(1 - p) = -ln(1/p - 1) = 2 * atanh(2p - 1)
properties.why: Follows directly from logarithm quotient rules, reciprocal transformation, and hyperbolic function identities

properties.property: Inversion via logistic function: logit^(-1)(alpha) = logistic(alpha) = 1 / (1 + e^(-alpha)) = e^alpha / (e^alpha + 1) = (tanh(alpha / 2) + 1) / 2
properties.why: The logit function is defined as the functional inverse of the standard logistic function

properties.property: Difference between logits equals the logarithm of the odds ratio: logit(p_1) - logit(p_2) = ln(R)
properties.why: The difference of the logarithms of the respective odds simplifies to the logarithm of the ratio of the odds

properties.property: Domain and range mapping: maps (0, 1) monotonically to (-inf, +inf)
properties.why: As p approaches 0 the log-odds tend to -infinity, and as p approaches 1 the log-odds tend to +infinity
Power series expansion of the logit function

properties.property: Role as canonical link and natural parameter: canonical link for the Bernoulli distribution and natural parameter for the binomial distribution
properties.why: Follows from generalized linear models and exponential family formulation

properties.property: Additive updates in state estimation: joint log-odds probabilities can be calculated by summing individual log-odds
properties.why: Logarithmic transformation replaces multiplication of small floating-point numbers with addition

assumptions.assumption: The probability argument p lies strictly within the open interval (0, 1)
assumptions.breaks_when: p <= 0 or p >= 1, causing division by zero in the odds ratio denominator (1 - p) or non-positive arguments to the logarithm

assumptions.assumption: The base of the logarithm is strictly greater than 1 (standardly base e)
assumptions.breaks_when: The base is less than or equal to 1 or negative, invalidating information units and monotonic ordering

failure_modes.mode: Boundary singularity at p = 0 or p = 1
failure_modes.signature: Evaluation yields -infinity, +infinity, or division-by-zero / NaN floating-point exceptions
failure_modes.cause: The odds denominator (1 - p) vanishes at p = 1 and the numerator vanishes at p = 0, where the natural logarithm diverges

failure_modes.mode: Numerical underflow and loss of significance near boundaries
failure_modes.signature: Catastrophic cancellation or 1 - p rounding to 1.0 (for tiny p) or p rounding to 1.0 (for p near 1)
failure_modes.cause: Finite floating-point precision cannot distinguish values arbitrarily close to 0 or 1 from the endpoints
